items.title: Happy World Television Day!
items.text: Every November 21, the UN celebrates TV. The day began in 1996, after the first World Television Forum. The idea: TV connects people all over the planet. So yes, today you have the perfect excuse to binge-watch!
items.mean: to watch many episodes of a show one after another
items.es: Hoy es el Día Mundial de la Televisión: ¡la tele conecta a personas de todo el mundo!
items.q: What show would you binge-watch this weekend, and why?

items.title: Four bright planets before breakfast
items.text: Wake up early this week and look east: Venus, Jupiter, Mars and Mercury are all in the sky before sunrise. Venus is the brightest, and it shines its best on November 24. It's a free show for early birds!
items.mean: people who get up very early in the morning
items.es: Esta semana se ven cuatro planetas brillantes antes del amanecer: ¡Venus, Júpiter, Marte y Mercurio!
items.q: Are you an early bird or a night owl? What do you like to do at that time?

items.title: Futa, the world's oldest red panda
items.text: Futa became famous in Japan in 2005 for standing up on two legs. Now he's 23, and Guinness World Records says he's the oldest red panda in captivity. Most live 12 to 17 years. He's even a great-great-grandfather!
items.mean: living in a zoo or a place made by people, not in nature
items.es: Futa, un panda rojo de Japón, es el más longevo del mundo: ¡tiene 23 años!
items.q: What's the oldest animal or pet you have ever known, and what was it like?

items.title: Happy World Children's Day!
items.text: Every November 20, kids in around 190 countries celebrate their rights. Some even take over adult jobs for a day, in TV, sport or business! Famous buildings like the Eiffel Tower light up in blue.
items.mean: to start doing a job or role that someone else usually does
items.es: Hoy es el Día Mundial de la Infancia: ¡los niños celebran sus derechos en todo el mundo!
items.q: If a child took over your job for one day, what do you think would happen?

items.title: Uranus is at its best this week
items.text: On November 25, Uranus reaches opposition: Earth is right between it and the Sun, so it shines its brightest all night. With a small telescope, you can spot a tiny green disc. Say hi to the ice giant!
items.mean: to see or notice something that is hard to see
items.es: Esta semana Urano está en su mejor momento: ¡se ve más brillante que nunca en el cielo nocturno!
items.q: What's the most amazing thing you've ever seen in the night sky?

items.title: Your cat meows to ask you for help
items.text: Scientists in Brazil put treats in a box that 38 cats couldn't open. Alone, the cats meowed 20 times in total. With a person there: 86 times! They also looked from the human to the box. Message: fix this, please!
items.mean: small, special pieces of food, often given as a reward
items.es: Un estudio en Brasil muestra que los gatos maúllan para pedirnos ayuda.
items.q: How do your pets, or the pets of people you know, ask for what they want?

items.title: Today is World Philosophy Day
items.text: Every third Thursday of November, UNESCO invites the world to think about big questions. What makes a good life? Why are we here? Grab a coffee and wonder a little: it's free and it's good for your brain!
items.mean: to think about something and ask yourself questions about it
items.es: Hoy es el Día Mundial de la Filosofía: ¡un día para pensar en las grandes preguntas!
items.q: What's a big question you sometimes think about when you're alone?

items.title: Voyager 1 is now one light-day away
items.text: Launched in 1977, NASA's Voyager 1 is now so far away that its radio messages take a full day to reach us. That's about 25.9 billion km! It's the most distant object humans have ever made.
items.es: La sonda Voyager 1 ya está a un día luz de la Tierra: ¡sus mensajes tardan un día en llegar!
items.q: If you could send one message to aliens far away, what would you say?

items.title: 430 steps up a mountain, built for Mom
items.text: In eastern China, an 86-year-old mom missed her mountain village, but the old path was overgrown. So her kids and family built 430 stone steps, some on a cliff, and even used a drone to carry stones. Now that's love!
items.mean: covered with too many plants that grew without control
items.es: Unos hermanos construyeron 430 escalones en una montaña para que su mamá pudiera volver a su pueblo.
items.q: What's something special your family did together, or something you did for someone you love?

items.title: Happy 98th birthday, Mickey Mouse!
items.text: On November 18, 1928, Mickey first appeared in "Steamboat Willie" at a theater in New York. It was a cartoon with sound, and Mickey made music with animals and pots on a boat. Not bad for a mouse!
items.mean: was seen for the first time
items.es: Mickey Mouse apareció por primera vez el 18 de noviembre de 1928, ¡hoy cumple 98 años!
items.q: What cartoon did you love as a child, and why did you like it so much?

items.title: The Moon visits Saturn on Friday
items.text: On Friday evening, look for the Moon: bright Saturn will be close to it in the sky. They'll be less than 6 degrees apart, so binoculars can show both together. A nice sky date for the weekend!
items.mean: a tool with two small tubes that makes far things look closer
items.es: El viernes en la noche, la Luna y Saturno se verán muy cerca en el cielo.
items.q: What's the best place you know for looking at the night sky?

items.title: Baby sea turtles, a California first
items.text: For the first time ever, sea turtles made nests on the US West Coast, in Southern California. Experts moved the eggs to an aquarium to keep them safe, and the tiny olive ridley hatchlings went back to the Pacific.
items.mean: baby animals that just came out of their eggs
items.es: Por primera vez, tortugas marinas anidaron en California y sus crías volvieron al Pacífico.
items.q: What's an animal you'd love to see in nature one day? Where would you go to see it?

items.title: It's Homemade Bread Day
items.text: In the US, November 17 is a day to bake your own bread at home. The idea is simple: flour, water, yeast, a warm kitchen and a lot of patience while the dough rises.
items.mean: flour and water mixed together, before you bake it
items.es: En EE. UU., el 17 de noviembre es el día de hornear tu propio pan en casa.
items.q: What's a bread or food from your country that everyone should try at least once?

items.title: Shooting stars tonight: the Leonids
items.text: The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight and tomorrow morning. Look up between midnight and dawn, far from city lights, and you might see a few meteors every hour. No telescope needed!
items.mean: the moment when the sun starts to come up
items.es: La lluvia de meteoros Leónidas llega a su punto máximo esta noche y mañana temprano.
items.q: Have you ever seen a shooting star? Where were you, and did you make a wish?

items.title: A coyote tried the world's biggest animal bridge first
items.text: Near Los Angeles, a huge bridge for wildlife goes over a 10-lane freeway. It opens officially on December 2, but cameras already caught a coyote walking across it. It couldn't wait!
items.mean: animals that live free in nature, not pets or farm animals
items.es: Cerca de Los Ángeles, un puente gigante para animales cruza una autopista. Una cámara ya captó a un coyote cruzándolo.
items.q: If you could build something to help animals in your city, what would it be?
